titleStmt.title: Emperor’s speech at the opening of the Prussian Parliament.

head.hi: Emperor’s speech at the opening of the Prussian Parliament.

div.p: Illustrious, Noble, and Honorable Gentlemen of both Houses of Parliament: In greeting the joint representation of the monarchy at the opening of a new legislative period, it is my heartfelt desire to again express my thanks through you to my people for the spontaneous expressions of affection and fealty to my house on the occasion of the birth of my great-grandson.

The increased activity among the industries resulting from the trade legislation of the imperial Government, combined with the general favorable results of the harvests, warrant the hope for a continued development of the welfare of all classes of the people.

The disproportion between the needs and means of the state, which for several years back has induced my Government to lay before the imperial Parliament bills for the introduction of new indirect taxes, still exists, owing to the repeated rejection of all these measures, and it is so considerable that it cannot be covered unless some new sources of revenue are opened up.

Even the limited margin to which the budget was restricted for the past year could not be covered without the aid of extraordinary means, and for the expenditures of the coming year, recourse will have to be had to the public credit, the necessary measures for which will be submitted for your approval, together with the budget.

Regarding the further needs of the state, my Government will endeavor, by the introduction of special measures, looking to the lightening of communal and school burdens, and the increase of the salaries of certain officials, in conjunction with other desirable organic innovations, to gain that sympathy and approval for the appropriation law covering the disposition of the surplus from the imperial revenue which have unfortunately until now been withheld. It is to be hoped that these necessities will receive due consideration, and that a budget may be mutually agreed upon, to the end that redressive imperial legislation may with better prospect of success be invoked.

In one direction, however, this time-wasting course cannot be pursued: the relief of the poorer classes of the population from the weight of the class tax must, in my opinion, be accomplished without delay.

It is my desire to see a stop put to the harsh and oppressive distraints arising from the collection of these taxes. A bill looking to the immediate and complete abolition of the four lower grades of class tax, and to the relief from the deficit thereby occasioned will be laid before you.

The system of nationalized railways has now been carried out in most parts of the Kingdom, and justifies, in my opinion, the greatest expectations, based on past results, which may be attached to these great measures. A bill for the construction of further important lines of railways in different parts of the Kingdom will be submitted.

A bill providing for the cutting of the first section of a canal designed to interunite the larger rivers in the western part of the Kingdom, and which was not passed upon at the last session, will be again submitted.

A bill will also be introduced looking to the simplification of the administrative organization in a manner rendered necessary by the exigencies of the times. By this measure, the reforms which have been begun, will be completed so as to permit of their being extended to the entire Kingdom.
A bill will be laid before you for remedying certain defects and hardships resulting from the writs of execution on real property.

It affords me satisfaction to announce that the re-establishment of diplomatic relations with the Roman Curia has been conducive to the strengthening of my friendly relations with the supreme head of the Catholic Church, and I cherish the hope that the conciliatory disposition which my Government will continue to manifest will also in the future exercise a beneficial influence upon the development of our ecclesiastico-political relations. Meanwhile my Government, acting in accordance with existing laws and the powers conferred upon it, will continue to extend to my Catholic subjects such indulgent consideration in ecclesiastical questions as may be consistent with the interests of the state and the nation.
It affords me special gratification to be able to announce to you that the relations of the German Empire to all foreign nations convince me that the blessings of peace will remain assured to us.

Gentlemen, again an extensive field of important work has been opened before you, and I express the hope that this work will, through your co-operation with my Government, also be, in this new session, fruitful of much good.
